plan.contextChunk: This figure sets four cylinder-and-piston drawings side by side as the successive steps of a cycle. Each cylinder holds a gray region stippled with dots for the gas, capped by a piston whose stem rises from the open top, and each stands inside a large colored block representing its surroundings. In the first, a red block labeled "Reservoir" and "(Temperature Th)" sends a thick gray arrow Qh upward into the gas while a green arrow W1 points up from the piston stem. The second sits in a pale block labeled "Insulation", green arrow W2 pointing up and the gas column taller. The third stands in a blue "Reservoir" block marked "(Temperature Tc)", with a green arrow W3 pointing down onto the piston and a gray arrow Qc leaving downward. The fourth returns to an "Insulation" block, with W4 pointing down and the gas at its shortest column. Bold captions run beneath: "Step 1: Isothermal expansion", "Step 2: Adiabatic expansion", "Step 3: Isothermal compression", and "Step 4: Adiabatic compression", each followed by a transition written M to N, N to O, O to P, and P to M. Left to right, block color, arrow direction, and gas volume shift together to track where heat crosses the boundary and which way work is done. The sequence lays out the four processes of the Carnot cycle for an ideal gas.

interactionPlan.concept: The Carnot cycle is four alternating isothermal (heat-crossing) and adiabatic (insulated) piston processes whose ordered expansion-then-compression motions trace a single closed loop on the p-V diagram.
elements: four vertical cylinder bodies arranged left to right (Steps 1-4)
four pistons with rising stems capping each gas column
four gray gas regions stippled with dots, heights varying: medium (Step 1), tallest (Step 2), medium (Step 3), shortest (Step 4)
Step 1 surrounding block: red, labeled 'Reservoir' and '(Temperature Th)'
Step 2 surrounding block: pale, labeled 'Insulation'
Step 3 surrounding block: blue, labeled 'Reservoir' and '(Temperature Tc)'
Step 4 surrounding block: pale, labeled 'Insulation'
heat arrow Qh: thick gray arrow pointing up into the gas (Step 1)
heat arrow Qc: thick gray arrow pointing down out of the gas (Step 3)
work arrows W1 and W2: green arrows pointing up from the piston stem (Steps 1-2, work done by gas)
work arrows W3 and W4: green arrows pointing down onto the piston (Steps 3-4, work done on gas)
bold captions under each panel: 'Step 1: Isothermal expansion (M→N)', 'Step 2: Adiabatic expansion (N→O)', 'Step 3: Isothermal compression (O→P)', 'Step 4: Adiabatic compression (P→M)'
p-V view: pressure (p) vertical axis and volume (V) horizontal axis
p-V view: closed MNOP loop with upper isotherm at Th (M→N), steeper adiabat (N→O), lower isotherm at Tc (O→P), steeper adiabat (P→M)
p-V view: point labels M, N, O, P at the four corners of the loop
p-V view: highlighted segment matching the currently selected step

interactions.label: Cycle step
interactions.teaches: Stepping through the cycle in order reveals the deliberate sequence isothermal-expansion, adiabatic-expansion, isothermal-compression, adiabatic-compression, and which reservoir or insulation each leg contacts

interactions.label: Process type
interactions.teaches: Heat arrows Qh and Qc exist only on the isothermal legs touching a reservoir; on the adiabatic legs the insulation block means no energy crosses the boundary as heat, so all energy change is work

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The same four physical piston motions map one-to-one onto the segments of the closed MNOP curve, so the enclosed loop area on the p-V diagram equals the net work of the cycle

demo_steps.title: The four legs in order
demo_steps.narration: Step through the cycle: each click advances one process, highlighting the active piston, its work arrow, and the reservoir or insulation block it sits in, making the expansion-then-compression ordering explicit.

demo_steps.title: Heat crosses only on isothermal legs
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the adiabatic view: Steps 2 and 4 light up inside insulation blocks with no heat arrow, while the isothermal view shows Qh entering at Th and Qc leaving at Tc — heat transfer is confined to the two reservoir legs.

demo_steps.title: Map piston motion to the p-V path
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to the p-V diagram and step through again: each selected cylinder state highlights the matching segment of the MNOP loop, showing the upper Th isotherm, lower Tc isotherm, and the two steeper adiabats connecting them.

demo_steps.title: Close the loop
demo_steps.narration: Advance to Step 4 (P→M): the final adiabat returns the gas to state M, closing the loop — the area enclosed by MNOP is the net work the engine delivers per cycle.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The Carnot cycle alternates heat-crossing isothermal legs with insulated adiabatic legs, and those same four piston motions draw a single closed loop on the p-V diagram whose enclosed area is the net work output.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Lay out four cylinder panels left to right, each a tall open-topped cylinder with a piston-and-stem cap and a dot-stippled gray gas column whose height encodes volume (Step 2 tallest, Step 4 shortest, Steps 1 and 3 medium). Surround each with a large colored block: red 'Reservoir (Temperature Th)' for Step 1, pale 'Insulation' for Step 2, blue 'Reservoir (Temperature Tc)' for Step 3, pale 'Insulation' for Step 4. Draw Qh as a thick gray up-arrow into the Step 1 gas and Qc as a thick gray down-arrow out of the Step 3 gas; draw W1, W2 as green up-arrows (work by gas) and W3, W4 as green down-arrows (work on gas). Bold step captions with M→N, N→O, O→P, P→M transitions sit beneath each panel. In p-V view, draw p (vertical) and V (horizontal) axes and a clockwise closed loop: a gentle upper isotherm M→N at Th, a steeper adiabat N→O, a gentle lower isotherm O→P at Tc, and a steeper adiabat P→M; label the four corner points and highlight the active segment in a strong accent color synced to stepButton. Cross-fade between the panel view and the p-V view on toggle rather than an abrupt swap.

Increase vertical spacing between the temperature label and the step caption — either move the temperature label up into the block or push captions down by ~20px to eliminate the collision
Use Unicode subscript characters (W₁, W₂, W₃, W₄) or SVG tspan with baseline-shift for the work labels to match the source typography
